title: Signed lattice Koszul totalization preserves derived triangles
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative condensed ring on the small coherent profinite site [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, def-weil-size-convention], let $r\geq0$, and put $D=\mathbf Z^r$, $\mathcal M=\operatorname{Mod}_R$ and $\mathcal E=\mathcal A_R(D)$ [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. Write $t:\mathcal M\to\mathcal E$ for trivial action and $\Gamma$ for invariants [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus]. Use ordinary derived categories and localization $Q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For equivariant cochain complexes use the finite Koszul complex of [lem-sfb-discrete-lattice-koszul-resolution] and its total $K(P)^n=\bigoplus_{a+b=n}K_R(P^b;T)^a$, with differential $d_K+(-1)^a d_P$. Each functor $K^a:\mathcal E\to\mathcal M$ is exact, and totalization is an additive functor on bounded-below complexes. It sends a homotopy $h$ to $H|_{K^a(P^b)}=(-1)^aK^a(h^b)$, preserves quasi-isomorphisms, and induces $\mathsf K:D^+(\mathcal E)\to D^+(\mathcal M)$. For every integer $n$ the shift comparison $K(P[n])\cong K(P)[n]$ acts by $(-1)^{an}$ in Koszul degree $a$ and is coherent with addition of shifts. For a cochain map $f:P\to P'$, with $\operatorname{Cone}(f)^m=P'^m\oplus P^{m+1}$ and differential $(y,x)\mapsto(dy+fx,-dx)$, the map $K(\operatorname{Cone}f)\cong\operatorname{Cone}(Kf)$ is identity on $K^a(P')$ and multiplication by $(-1)^a$ on $K^a(P[1])$. These are natural chain isomorphisms compatible with cone inclusion and projection (and hence with the cone triangle's signed last arrow). With these comparisons $\mathsf K$ is triangulated. A termwise short exact sequence of input complexes remains termwise short exact after $K$; its canonical connecting arrow is carried by this triangle comparison.

source.place: Paragraph (3), ordinary open direct image; agent-formulated lattice expansion, returned proof steps 1–3: exact finite totalization, homotopy, quasi-isomorphisms, shifts and cones. The blueprint supplies the route, not this structural calculation.

proof.text: Let $U:\mathcal E\to\mathcal M$ forget the action. By [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus], $U$ is additive and exact and both categories are abelian. The formula in [lem-sfb-discrete-lattice-koszul-resolution] identifies $K^a$ with $\binom ra$ copies of $U$ for $0\leq a\leq r$, and zero otherwise. Kernels and cokernels of a finite direct sum of maps are the direct sums of their kernels and cokernels (the component projections and inclusions give the universal properties). Thus these functors are additive and exact. The same component calculation shows that a termwise short exact sequence stays termwise short exact after taking the finite diagonal sums defining $K$. In the Lean implementation, the term functor is naturally isomorphic to the action-forgetting functor followed by the finite constant diagram and its limit. The biproduct comparison identifies this limit functor with the corresponding colimit functor, proving preservation of finite limits and colimits. To handle the chosen coproduct presentation of each total degree directly, use that internal modules are Grothendieck abelian (the trivial-group case of the restriction calculus): AB5 implies AB4, so the coproduct functor on the diagonal diagrams is exact. The diagram functor is exact after every evaluation, by the term calculation. Their composite is naturally isomorphic to evaluation of the total; transport short exactness through this isomorphism.

source.place: Agent expansion of paragraph (3): exact finite sums; compare homology.tex Tag 012Z, definition-associated-simple-complex.

proof.text: Put $B(P)^{a,b}=K_R(P^b;T)^a$, with horizontal differential $d_K$ and vertical differential $d_P$. The Koszul formula of [lem-sfb-discrete-lattice-koszul-resolution] and equivariance give $d_K^2=0$ and $d_Kd_P=d_Pd_K$. Hence $(d_K+(-1)^ad_P)^2=0$: the mixed terms have coefficients $(-1)^{a+1}$ and $(-1)^a$. For a cochain map $f$, use $K^a(f^b)$ on each summand; it commutes with both differentials. Identities, composition and addition hold on each summand. Only $0\leq a\leq r$ contribute in any total degree. If $P^b=0$ for $b<N$, then $K(P)^n=0$ for $n<N$. Thus the stated finite totalization is an additive functor on bounded-below complexes.

source.place: Agent expansion of paragraph (3): finite signed totalization; homology.tex Tag 012Z, definition-associated-simple-complex.

proof.text: For an equivariant cochain homotopy $h$ with $f-g=d_{P'}h+hd_P$, set $H|_{B(P)^{a,b}}=(-1)^aK^a(h^b)$. In $dH+Hd$ the horizontal terms are $(-1)^ad_Kh+(-1)^{a+1}hd_K=0$, since $h$ is equivariant. The vertical terms are $d_{P'}h+hd_P$ on each summand, giving $K(f)-K(g)$. This proves the homotopy formula, so $K$ also acts on the bounded-below homotopy category (the homotopy convention is that used in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]). The Lean proof constructs this homotopy for an arbitrary additive complex-valued functor and specializes it to the Koszul functor. The calculation follows the existing private helper additiveComplexFunctor_total_map_homotopy in WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.AlternatingCechTotalHomotopy, retaining the explicit summand formula in its conclusion.

source.place: Agent expansion of paragraph (3): direct signed homotopy calculation.

proof.text: If $f$ is a quasi-isomorphism, exactness of each $K^a$ and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] show that $K^a(f)$ is a quasi-isomorphism of vertical complexes. Apply [lem-sc-integer-finite-column-total-comparison] to $B(f)$, with integer column bounds $x_0=0$, $x_1=r$. Both double complexes have zero columns outside these bounds; their diagonal totals exist by the finite sums of step 2. Its conclusion is precisely that $K(f)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The localization universal property in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] therefore gives $\mathsf K:D^+(\mathcal E)\to D^+(\mathcal M)$; the lower bound verified in step 2 ensures this codomain.

source.place: Agent expansion of paragraph (3): finite-column comparison; homology.tex Tag 010N, lemma-exact-functor; integer finite-column theorem in BicomplexColumns.lean:939.

proof.text: For $n\in\mathbf Z$, define $c_n:K(P[n])\to K(P)[n]$ by the sign $s_a=(-1)^{an}$ on Koszul degree $a$, using the shift convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The source differential is $d_K+(-1)^{a+n}d_P$; the target differential is $(-1)^nd_K+(-1)^{a+n}d_P$. The horizontal chain equation is $s_{a+1}=(-1)^ns_a$, and the vertical equation uses the same $s_a$ at both ends. Thus $c_n$ is a chain isomorphism, with inverse given by the same signs. These scalar maps commute with every $K(f)$, so are natural. Also $c_0=1$ and $(-1)^{an}(-1)^{am}=(-1)^{a(n+m)}$ give coherence for all integer shifts, including negative ones. The existing totalShiftIsoApp is the total of mapCochainComplexShiftIso followed by totalShift₂Iso. On a summand the former has identity components; the latter has the required signed inclusion formula. Thus no new shift construction is needed.

source.place: Agent expansion of paragraph (3): shift comparison; homology.tex Tag 011G, definition-shift-cochain. Compare TotalComplexShift.lean:313.

proof.text: Use the cone convention in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Reorder the finite summands of $K(\operatorname{Cone}f)$ into those from $P'$ and those from $P[1]$. Define $\theta_f$ to be identity on the first group and $s_a=(-1)^a$ on the second. On an input $x$ in the second group, the source differential has components $s_af(x)$ in the first group and $d_Kx-s_ad_Px$ in the second. Applying $\theta_f$ to that differential gives $s_af(x)$ and $-s_ad_Kx-d_Px$, respectively, exactly the differential of $(0,s_ax)$ in $\operatorname{Cone}(Kf)$. The first group already has the differential of $K(P')$. Thus $\theta_f$ is a chain isomorphism with the stated inverse. Naturality follows because all component maps commute with the scalar signs. With $i,p$ and $i_K,p_K$ the cone inclusion and projection, these same component formulas give $\theta_f K(i)=i_K$ and $p_K\theta_f=c_1K(p)$, hence also $(-p_K)\theta_f=c_1K(-p)$.

source.place: Agent expansion of paragraph (3): cone comparison and signed last arrow; derived.tex Tag 014E, definition-cone.

proof.text: The natural shift isomorphisms descend through localization, since their components are already chain isomorphisms. By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], distinguished triangles are the triangles isomorphic to localized cone triangles with last arrow $-p$. Step 6 identifies the image of each such triangle under $\mathsf K$, using $c_1$ on its final vertex, with the cone triangle of $K(f)$, including its last arrow. Isomorphic triangles retain this property. Here $D^+$ is, as in the statement, the localization of bounded-below complexes at quasi-isomorphisms, so its distinguished triangles are those isomorphic to localized cone triangles of chain maps $f$ between bounded-below complexes; the cone of such an $f$ is again bounded below, so steps 2–6 apply to it. (Those steps use no lower bound at all, so the same argument also gives a triangulated $\mathsf K:D(\mathcal E)\to D(\mathcal M)$.) This proves that $\mathsf K$ is triangulated, in exactly the sense of [def-weil-triangulated-category].

source.place: Agent expansion of paragraph (3): cone criterion for the triangulated structure on ordinary derived categories.

proof.text: For a termwise short exact sequence $0\to A\xrightarrow{i}B\xrightarrow{j}C\to0$ let $i_c:B\to\operatorname{Cone}(i)$ and $p:\operatorname{Cone}(i)\to A[1]$ be the cone inclusion and projection, and let $q:\operatorname{Cone}(i)\to C$ be $(j,0)$, a chain map because $ji=0$. By [lem-pc-cone-short-exact-quasi-iso], $q$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The canonical connecting arrow of the sequence is, by definition, $\delta=Q(-p)Q(q)^{-1}:C\to A[1]$ (Stacks Tag 0152, $\delta=-p\circ q^{-1}$; this is also the arrow of Mathlib's DerivedCategory.triangleOfSES). Since $qi_c=j$ and $\delta Q(q)=Q(-p)$, the triple $(1,1,Q(q))$ is an isomorphism from the localized cone triangle $(Q(i),Q(i_c),Q(-p))$ to $(Q(i),Q(j),\delta)$, so the latter is distinguished by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The image sequence $0\to KA\to KB\to KC\to0$ is termwise exact by step 1; write $p_K,q_K$ for its cone projection and its map $(Kj,0)$, so its canonical arrow is $\delta_K=Q(-p_K)Q(q_K)^{-1}$, with $q_K$ a quasi-isomorphism by the same node. On the two summand groups $q_K\theta_i=K(q)$: on the first it is $K(j)$ and on the second it is zero. $K(q)$ is a quasi-isomorphism by step 4, and $\mathsf K(Q(q))=Q(Kq)$, $\mathsf K(Q(-p))=Q(K(-p))$ by construction of $\mathsf K$. Together with $(-p_K)\theta_i=c_1K(-p)$ from step 6, $c_1\mathsf K(\delta)=Q(-p_K)Q(\theta_i)Q(Kq)^{-1}=Q(-p_K)Q(q_K)^{-1}=\delta_K$, using $Q(q_K)Q(\theta_i)=Q(Kq)$ and invertibility of $Q(\theta_i)$. This is the canonical connecting arrow for the image sequence, proving the final compatibility without a choice of degreewise splittings.
